_meta_itemized.notes: THIS FILING'S PAGES ARE A COLOR PHOTOGRAPH OF THE ORIGINAL PAPER (shot on a wooden table, page edges and shadow visible, blue ballpoint legible) - not a photocopy. That makes it by far the most legible copy of Franchek's ledger and it is the reason this record's reads are high-confidence where 20650's are not. THE SUBSTANTIVE FINDING, AND IT IS A SOURCE PROPERTY THE BRIEFS DO NOT LIST: the Post-Election filing (this document) RE-SUBMITS THE PRE-ELECTION FILING'S SCHEDULE PAGES VERBATIM - the same single self-contribution, the same three expenses, the same handwritten totals, the same corrections in the same places as 20650, and identical cover figures (contributions $500, expenditures $503.02, balance $3.02). Cover-differencing the pair therefore gives zero new activity between the two reports, which is the pair gate the chunk brief asked for and it holds. The two documents are transcribed independently (each record is read from its own pages), but a consumer counting Franchek's 2022 money must not add the two filings together. Address handling: the p2 donor row's Mailing Address cell holds a street address with a unit number and NO city or state (the sheet's separate Zipcode cell is filled), so donor_city/donor_state are honestly BLANK - not redacted, simply not written, and a city is never inferred from a zip. GEOMETRY: p2 is DECLARED - rowbands finds no rules above y=30% on that page, so the frame (y0 17.00, pitch 1.91) comes from a direct dark-row probe of the 14-32% window, which returns a regular run of rules at 17.00, 18.93, 20.73, 22.66, 24.52, 26.41, 28.32, 30.25 (fitgrid independently reports pitch 1.9124 explaining 35 of 36 detected rules, mean residual 0.09); band 4 was crop-verified to frame the Franchek row. p3 is MEASURED (bands 4/5/6 = the three written rows, crop-verified), with one honest caveat: on that page the writing crosses the printed rules, so each measured band begins AT its row's text and extends down through the blank band beneath it - the box contains its row, but at the top edge rather than centred.
